changelog_1_2: Added replacement_cost_doctrine (top-level) + a per-cluster replacement_cost block to all 9 clusters. Driven by a 2026-07-14 finding that ORA's operative basis-floor benchmarks ($140 Midwest / $170 MD / $150 Richmond / $130 DSM) were NEVER SOURCED — and the basis floor is the primary acquisition gate. Sourcing pass produced defensible (DERIVED) hard-cost figures for only 3 of 9 metros; the other 6 are recorded as UNSOURCED rather than interpolated. Operative benchmarks retained UNCHANGED for scoring continuity but flagged PROVISIONAL/UNRATIFIED and likely TOO LOW. Also added: KC flood-district DD flag, Montgomery County MD coverage downgrade (monthly), Madison thin-inventory confirmation.
owner: Gabriel Goldberg, Principal, Oxford Realty Advisors

scoring_rule.note: Entry-phase clusters score 4 ('new target market'), NOT 1 ('isolated'); they graduate to 6 once a beachhead property closes. No prior new-market penalty applies to any listed cluster.

replacement_cost_doctrine.status: PROVISIONAL — UNRATIFIED. Added 2026-07-14 after a sourcing pass established that ORA's operative benchmarks were never sourced. DO NOT treat operative_benchmark_psf as ratified fact.
replacement_cost_doctrine.why_this_matters: The buy-box basis hard floor (>=25% discount to replacement cost) is the PRIMARY gate on every acquisition. The replacement-cost figure IS the gate. An unsourced benchmark means an unsourced gate — deals are being passed and pursued on a number nobody verified.

definitions.hard_cost_psf: Shell (tilt-up or PEMB, 20-28ft clear) + site work + basic office finish. EXCLUDES land, soft costs, developer fee.
definitions.all_in_psf: Hard cost + land + soft costs (A&E, permits, construction-period interest, insurance) + developer fee. THIS is the figure the basis test should use, because we compare it to a purchase price for an existing building ON ITS LAND. Conflating hard cost with all-in is the main failure mode.
definitions.which_one_do_we_use: UNRESOLVED — Gabriel to rule. The operative benchmarks below were never labelled as either, which is itself the problem.

operative_benchmark_psf.provenance: UNSOURCED. These are the figures the ora-deal-sourcing-scan has been running on. They are retained ONLY to keep scoring continuous week-over-week, NOT because they are validated.
operative_benchmark_psf.known_bias: LIKELY TOO LOW, not too high. Cushman & Wakefield's 2025 Industrial Construction Cost Guide prices a 'small' ground-up project at $139/SF — but its 'small' tier is a 109,200 SF building, more than 2x ORA's typical sub-50K SF target. Multiple sources (Bisnow Sept 2025 re: Penntex; NAIOP Spring 2026 small-bay coverage) put TRUE small-bay/multi-tenant flex construction at $160-220/SF, because small floor plates carry far more demising wall, HVAC zoning, and doors per SF than a bulk box. If the correct Midwest figure is ~$170 rather than $140, the basis floor moves from <=$105/SF to <=$127/SF and MULTIPLE DEALS PREVIOUSLY DECLINED ON BASIS WOULD CLEAR IT.
operative_benchmark_psf.sensitivity_evidence: On the 2026-07-14 scan, moving the Midwest benchmark from $140 to $170 flips 1885-1895 S High St ($119.32), 1100 W Town St ($112.98), 2450 Production Dr ($122.84), and 1401 Minnesota Ave ($116.14) from FAIL-BASIS to PASS. That is 4 deals turned by one unsourced assumption.

replacement_cost_doctrine.how_to_ratify: The authoritative primary source is the Cushman & Wakefield Industrial Construction Cost Guide (46-market table, published ~annually). It is behind a lead-gen download at cushmanwakefield.com/en/united-states/insights/industrial-construction-cost-guide and CANNOT be fetched by an agent. ACTION FOR GABRIEL: download it once, drop the metro table into this file, and the benchmarks become sourced. Secondary path: ask a GC or a lender in each core market for a current all-in $/SF on a 30-50K SF shallow-bay build — a two-email exercise that would beat every public source found.
replacement_cost_doctrine.staleness_warning: Construction cost is reaccelerating hard in 2026: Turner Building Cost Index +4.87% YoY (Q1 2026); Mortenson +6.77% YoY (Q1 2026); AGC nonresidential input PPI +8.4% YoY through May 2026 — largest since the pandemic — on tariff-driven steel (+20.7%), aluminum (+33.0%), copper (+20.9%). Materials are moving faster than labor, which matters MORE for shallow-bay/PEMB product where materials are a larger share of shell cost. A benchmark older than ~12 months is understating current cost by high single digits. RE-CHECK QUARTERLY.
replacement_cost_doctrine.research_provenance: 9-metro sourcing pass run 2026-07-14 (59 tool calls). Defensible hard-cost figures were obtained for only 3 of 9 metros, all [DERIVED]. Six metros returned NO defensible source. Recorded honestly per-cluster below rather than interpolated — an explicit gap is more useful than a fabricated number.

clusters.flood_note: STANDING DD FLAG (added 2026-07-14): the Kaw River bottoms districts — Fairfax Industrial Park, Armourdale, West Bottoms — sit behind the UG/USACE levee system and are the same districts devastated in the 1951 'Black Friday' flood; levee improvement is still active as of July 2026. Cheap $/SF in these submarkets frequently reflects flood exposure, not mispricing. Pull a FEMA flood-zone determination and a flood-insurance quote BEFORE underwriting any KCK/West Bottoms basis play.
